# Calendar

Month, week, and day views over the same MOTE substrate as everything else — events are just
`kind = calendar` MOTEs synced via JMAP alongside mail, chat, and contacts. There is no separate
central calendar service to trust or to lose.

![Calendar — month view](assets/screens/calendar-dark.png)

## Getting around

Open **Calendar** from the left rail. Switch between **Month**, **Week**, and **Day** views from
the header, and use the always-visible **agenda** rail for a fast "today / this week" read
without changing view:

![Calendar — agenda view](assets/screens/calendar-agenda-dark.png)

## Creating an event

Click any day/slot, or the **New event** button. Fill in a title, time (or toggle **all-day**),
and an optional reminder (at start, 10/30 min, 1 hour, or 1 day before). Set it to **repeat** for
a recurring event.

## Inviting people

Add attendees straight from your [Contacts](#contacts) list while creating or editing an event —
an event with invitees becomes a **meeting**, and the client marks it as such. Inviting someone
sends a **signed MOTE, not a server request** — the same iTIP-style invite/accept/decline/tentative
flow existing calendar tools use, carried over the mesh instead of a shared server. Free/busy is
answered the same way: a message, not a query against a central calendar database.

**Responding to an invite:** an invitation shows up as a banner at the top of the relevant thread
in Mail, or directly in Calendar with a badge on the pending event. Click **Yes**, **Maybe**, or
**No** — your RSVP is itself a signed MOTE sent back to the organizer, and their view of the event
updates once it arrives.

## How it interoperates

- **Native** — JSCalendar (RFC 8984) objects synced via JMAP, end-to-end encrypted at rest and in
  transit like every other MOTE kind.
- **Compatibility** — a CalDAV (RFC 4791) server projects the same event store as iCalendar for
  Apple Calendar, Thunderbird, and other CalDAV clients, so switching to Envoir doesn't mean
  switching calendar apps on day one. See
  [JMAP/IMAP/CalDAV client setup](#client-setup) for connecting one, and
  [Mail](#mail#client-protocols) for the client-protocol picture shared with mail.

## What's real vs. simulated today

Event **construction** (a real signed MOTE, exactly like a mail or chat message) and the full UI —
month/week/day rendering, recurrence, reminders, the invite/RSVP flow — are real code in the web
client. As with every other module, **delivery** of that MOTE across the mesh is the same
clearly-labeled in-browser simulation described in
[`client/README.md`](https://github.com/vul-os/envoir/blob/main/client/README.md); the seed events you see on first load are demo data,
not a real calendar. See [Roadmap](#roadmap) for the project-wide real-vs-simulated line.
